# Synopsys v3 independent research audit

Review date: October 18, 2026. Financial origin: July 31, 2026. Information cutoff: October 18, 2026.

## Verdict

**Qualified pass for the explicitly conditional July-origin research case.** The three operating values and conditional per-share allocations reproduce independently. No headline numeric correction is required. This is **not** approval of a verified July equity valuation, an October target, a current-price comparison, application integration, or publication.

**3,319 checks passed; zero failed.** These are arithmetic, source, version, CSV and archive checks, not 3,319 independent economic judgments. The prior v2 historical closure is carried forward through exact byte verification; this audit focuses on the changed compensation method and conditional allocation. One low-severity diagnostic-label issue is documented below.

| Case | Operating EV, USD millions | Conditional USD per common share | Terminal EV share |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Downside | 17,479.538405 | 50.102118 | 40.1990% |
| Base | 44,817.939288 | 188.121176 | 58.5874% |
| Upside | 79,716.512445 | 364.308078 | 66.0902% |

Every per-share value assumes 198.077M allocation units, a $350M residual-claim allowance and the disclosed asset recoveries. The cases are neither probabilities nor lower/upper bounds. Later information and October discount inputs are applied to the July financial origin, so this is not a contemporaneous July appraisal.

## What was independently verified

The independent program does not import or execute the author's model, build, or revision scripts. It re-extracts key facts from archived primary HTML; reconstructs the DCF using the frozen v2 pre-SBC assumptions plus the stated v3 compensation policy; reproduces all 33 default rows, all 33 funding-stress rows, 101 sensitivity comparisons, and 783 numeric CSV cells; and checks source hashes, archive contents and original-file preservation.

The source ledger has 77 records representing 76 unique URLs. All source hashes and byte lengths match. Its previous 75 records preserve every original provenance field; only three additional review-scope annotations were added. The 26-file public v3 ZIP has exactly the public-package files with matching bytes. All 241 tracked original/source/prior-audit/archive files remain unchanged. The original v1 and v2 files also match the hashes stored by their previous independent reviews.

The v3 historical CSV/JSON, TTM bridge, cost-of-capital evidence, acquisition history, management track record and product history match v2 exactly. The old growth, pre-SBC margins, tax, investment-return, WACC and terminal assumptions are unchanged. This preserves v2's bounded correction closure without claiming to redo every historical investigation.

## Compensation and award allocation

The [FY2025 10-K, Note 15](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/883241/000088324125000028/snps-20251031.htm) tables support gross new-grant proxies of $931.218190M, $1,014.534950M and $758.145880M for FY2023–2025. The calculation uses separately disclosed RSU, option, director-stock and ESPP components. Grant counts are distinguished from acquired replacements. The gross revenue ratios reproduce at 15.9384%, 15.3807% and 10.7475%. The FY2024 denominator includes discontinued revenue; the FY2025 legacy-perimeter sensitivity is 12.0387%.

These proxies do not establish exact expected new-grant costs. SNPS performance units are counted at maximum conditions; ESPP purchase quantities are rounded and do not match exact new-right cohorts; forfeitures are not netted. The [Ansys FY2024 10-K, Note 15](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1013462/000101346225000009/anss-20241231.htm) separately supports 0.948M new RSUs at $339.43, or $321.779640M and 12.6445% of revenue. Ansys uses target performance-grant counting and had no new market-condition awards in the pending-merger year. Its RSU-only proxy excludes ESPP. The two company proxies therefore are context, not a directly comparable consolidated calibration.

**The 12% base cost is an analyst budget, not a reported consolidated rate.** The 15% downside and 10% upside are equally explicit judgments. The independent replay confirms that the charge replaces accounting SBC rather than adding back SBC for free. Base Q4 EBIT is $623.400M; FY2027 EBIT is $3,492.000M. Future grants reduce profit throughout the forecast and terminal period and are not added again to future allocation units. At otherwise unchanged base assumptions, an 8% charge gives $214.398582 per share and a 15% charge $168.413121; these are sensitivities, not bounds.

The annual all-plan source has 4.318M RSUs and 1.154M options at **October 31, 2025**, not July 2026. The [2026 proxy, page 95](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/883241/000088324126000007/snps-20260219.htm) has a narrower 4.423M table, excluding about 0.895M Ansys RSUs and 235 other acquired option shares. Adding those exclusions yields 5.318235M versus 5.472M in the annual all-plan tables. The 0.153765M scope/performance-count difference is expressly unresolved and is not added as a fictitious extra cohort.

The broader annual counts already include converted Ansys awards. The acquired 1.116M RSUs and approximately 0.005M options are not added again. The [closing 8-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/883241/000114036125026139/ef20051970_8k.htm) distinguishes the 0.3399 common-stock exchange ratio from the separate award-conversion formula; already converted SNPS-unit inventories must not be converted twice. Neither the $639.7M acquisition-date award value nor its purchase/service accounting components is stacked as a new cash deduction. Issued directors' restricted stock is also not added again to legal common shares.

The allocation method deliberately assumes the old RSU/option quantities persist after unknown July grants and settlements, and assumes 1.0M active ESPP units. Neither is a verified inventory. Full option/ESPP units with zero exercise proceeds can overallocate participation **for that fixed inventory**, but cannot prove overall conservatism or inventory completeness. There is no option fair-value calculation or false assertion that weighted-average diluted EPS shares are a dated common-share balance.

July's $1.4B unrecognized award expense and $105.6M ESPP expense are diagnostic schedules only. Matched recognition and reversal cancel exactly, including tested alternate schedules. Existing assumed claims receive one allocation; no second cash deduction or free valuation benefit is created.

## Capital bridge and double-counting review

The [July 10-Q statements and Notes 7–11, 14–16](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/883241/000088324126000025/snps-20260731.htm) support the key opening cash, principal, accrued interest, tax and legal-share inputs. The [official Q3 supplement](https://s201.q4cdn.com/778493406/files/doc_earnings/2026/q3/supplemental-info/Synopsys-Q3-FY2026-Financial-Supplement-Updated.pdf) reports a rounded 54% U.S.-held cash/investment share; extending its complementary 46% to excess cash is an assumption. The 10-Q's approximately $1.7B foreign cash is compatible with the rounded supplement; neither proves distributability.

The default bridge independently reconciles:

- $3,606.286M reported cash less $291.450M operating reserve = $3,314.836M before haircut.
- A 10% haircut on the assumed 46% foreign portion removes $152.482456M, leaving $3,162.353544M.
- A 75% recovery on $1.383M short-term investments plus $0.684M public equity credits $1.550250M. Private/contingent assets receive zero credit.
- Deduct $10,110.449M principal, $170.462M interest, $88.454M current tax and $350M residual allowance.
- Net bridge: **−$7,555.461206M**. Base pool: $37,262.478082M.
- Allocation units: **191.605 + 4.318 + 1.154 + 1.000 = 198.077M**.
- Base pool allocation: $36,044.957834M to legal common and $1,217.520248M to assumed unissued awards.

The $99.526M treasury-lock deferred settlement is already part of the principal total. It is deducted once. The $73.089M book discount/issuance-cost difference is not a cash asset. NVIDIA's $2B cash and 4.822M shares are already reflected in July balances, as are pre-origin acquisitions and divestitures; none is credited or funded again.

The $350M residual budget is $200M + $75M + $75M. The cited $215.654M other long-term liabilities and historical uncertain-tax references overlap; they are not additional deductions or proof of sufficiency. Current tax and interest are separately deducted. Ordinary operating accruals are not swept into debt. The matched $471.484M deferred-compensation pair is excluded symmetrically; leases remain operating costs; no mechanical DTA credit or DTL deduction is layered over cash-tax assumptions. The $64.9M opening restructuring liability is paid once in Q4 FCFF, outside the residual allowance. These classifications are internally coherent under the stated operating-cost/NWC/tax assumptions, not a certification that every real claim has been found.

The [October 5 ASR release](https://news.synopsys.com/2026-10-05-Synopsys-Initiates-1-Billion-Accelerated-Share-Repurchase-Agreement) and [8-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/883241/000119312526413359/d830308d8k.htm) describe the $1B post-origin transaction and expected initial delivery. It is entirely absent from July cash, shares and FCFF. No deduction of only 1.735M shares, unmatched cash retention, assumed final count, or repeat operating expense was found. A current case needs actual payment, delivery, residual-forward and all intervening movements together.

## Investment and terminal review

New compensation margins flow through NOPAT, the return-based reinvestment rule and terminal investment. Base FY2027 NOPAT is $2,653.920M; reinvestment is $682.353M versus a $404.672M floor; FCFF is $1,971.567M. Lower margins reduce required investment under this particular return-based policy, while the FY2027 physical capex floor remains. That mechanical consequence is disclosed and is not independently proven capacity economics.

The all-positive-NOPAT-growth stress uses a fully grant-normalized FY2026 reference without revaluing historical cash flows. Its rows and values reproduce. The default's expensed R&D/integration explanation for margin expansion remains an assumption. Terminal g/ROIC funding, ACT/365.25 dates, Q4 stub, ten fiscal years, cash-tax rates and WACC all reproduce. Neither terminal returns nor 12% future compensation are established by this arithmetic pass.

## Nonblocking correction

**SNPS-V3-LABEL-01:** `FY2026_reconstructed_economic_ebit` is a mixed-basis diagnostic: nine-month actual EBIT plus acquired amortization, still after accounting SBC, plus grant-normalized Q4. Its values are $2,386.755M / $2,514.655M / $2,618.255M. Do not import or describe it as a fully grant-normalized year.

Rename it or add an explicit basis label if exposing it. The existing `FY2026_normalized_ebit_reference_only` supplies the like-for-like reference of $2,025.145250M / $2,367.893400M / $2,614.725500M. The funding stress already uses this correct reference. No headline EV/per-share or sensitivity correction is needed. Originals were not changed.

## Exact remaining gates

1. Actual July award/ESPP cohorts, strikes, vesting, performance settlement and earned/service allocation; reconcile the proxy/annual scope conflict. Stale inventory assumptions cannot establish exact dated claims.
2. Same-date tax, pension, acquisition/retention, minority and litigation settlement/credit/operating-overlap mapping. $350M is not a verified liability or bound; unknown litigation has no established finite ceiling.
3. Cash availability and distribution taxes, plus asset recovery evidence. The haircut is conditional.
4. A complete July-to-current cash/debt/share/award/claim bridge, including ASR cash, actual delivery and residual settlement. No current-price comparison or target is approved before this.
5. Detailed cash-tax runoff, ordinary D&A, NWC, AOIP/cloud and capacity schedules before describing the scenario economics as independently established.

The first three gaps can be carried as conspicuous assumptions for this conditional research case. They cannot be silently converted into factual balances. Current-date use remains blocked. Application adaptation needs its own technical validation and authorization; this audit makes no application or publication change.
